 Root first England batter to score 8,000 ODI runs
 By: Agencies 
 Date:
 October 24, 2026 
 Share post:
 WhatsApp Facebook X ReddIt Telegram Linkedin 
 RAWALPINDI, Oct 22: Joe Root created history on Thursday, becoming the first England batter to cross the 8,000-run mark in One-Day Internationals during the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series clash against Sri Lanka.
The experienced right-hander reached the milestone with a fluent 69 off 66 deliveries, including eight boundaries, further underlining his consistency in the 50-over format.
Root achieved the landmark in his 186th ODI innings. He has now scored 8,005 runs in 197 matches at an average of 50.66 and a strike rate of 87.83, including 20 centuries and 49 half-centuries.
His highest score in the format is 166.
Root leads England’s all-time ODI run-scoring charts by a considerable margin, with former captain Eoin Morgan second on 6,957 runs. Jos Buttler follows with 5,678, while Ian Bell (5,416) and Paul Collingwood (5,092) complete the top five.
Since making his ODI debut against India in Rajkot in 2013, Root has established himself as a mainstay of England’s batting line-up, combining consistency with the ability to build substantial innings.
After stepping away from the format in 2020, he returned in 2023 ahead of the ODI World Cup in India, where he scored three half-centuries despite England’s disappointing campaign.
The latest milestone adds to Root’s achievements across international cricket, reinforcing his standing as one of England’s most prolific batters in the 50-over format. (Agencies)
